full_prompt_html:
Act as an IT service manager, a systems administrator and a security analyst.

Our support queue is growing faster than we can clear it. Triage the backlog and tell us what to work on first. [Paste an export of open tickets with ID, title, description, requester, date opened and status.] [State how many people work the queue and any service-level targets you have.]

Work through the backlog in four steps:

1. Group and Deduplicate

  • Group the tickets that describe the same underlying problem, and list the ticket IDs in each group.
  • Identify duplicates that can be closed with a reference to one master ticket.
  • Name the five most common root causes across the backlog.

2. Prioritize

  • Score each ticket or group for impact (how many people, which business processes) and urgency (deadline, and whether a workaround exists).
  • Flag every ticket that describes a possible security issue, such as suspicious sign-ins, phishing, lost devices or shared credentials, and move it to the top.
  • Identify tickets older than 30 days that no one has updated.

3. Fix the Source, Not Only the Tickets

  • For each common root cause, suggest one permanent fix, such as a configuration change, a knowledge-base article or a self-service form.
  • Estimate how many future tickets each fix would remove.

4. Plan the Work

  • Propose a two-week plan that spreads the work across the team, based on the capacity I gave you.
  • List the tickets that should be closed, deferred or escalated, with a one-line reason for each.

Deliver a ranked table with columns for Group, Ticket IDs, Impact, Urgency, Priority and Action, followed by the root-cause fixes and the two-week plan. State every assumption you made about missing data.
summary: Triage an IT support backlog by grouping duplicates, ranking impact and urgency, surfacing security issues, fixing root causes, and planning capacity.
title: Triage your IT support backlog into a ranked plan
